newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU aid to Ireland to be trimmed - RTE.
newsitem.headline: EU aid to Ireland to be trimmed - RTE.

text.p: EU Commission President Jacques Santer is to recommend a reduction in grants and aid to Ireland, a key component in its booming economy, state broadcaster RTE reported on Friday.
Its Brussels correspondent said Santer would outline his plans in an address to the European Parliament on July 16 covering a reform of EU structural funds and its Common Agricultural policy (CAP).
The report said Santer's proposals would be linked to the eventual enlargement of the bloc to include former Communist states.
By its account, the former Irish government of John Bruton was aware of Santer's proposals and had worked out a negotiating stance. There was no confirmation of the report in Dublin.

The report said Santer would point out that Ireland's economy has performed so well that average wealth is approaching that of the EU's major economies and that the country no longer qualified for aid.
It said Bruton's administration had asked for the grants to be extended for one final five-year period beyond a 1999 cutoff date.
CAP grants and loans to farmers would also be trimmed because of a long period of agricultural modernisation.

Ireland has been earmarked around six billion ECUs ($6.7 billion) worth of aid over the past few years which account for some three percent of Gross Domestic Product, according to Bruton's government.

Bruton's centre-left coalition was defeated in June 6 elections and the report said that a renegotiation of Dublin's aid entitlement would be a major challenge for Prime Minister Bertie Ahern's centre-right coalition.
